reading.body:
Manus AI, founded in 2025, builds an autonomous agent positioned to execute tasks and automate workflows on a user's behalf rather than merely provide information, marking a shift toward AI systems with direct operational impact.

The distinction matters for understanding AI's infrastructure demands. An information-retrieval system like a chatbot can run inference on modest hardware and sit idle between queries. An autonomous agent that executes tasks, integrates with email and Slack, and generates images must maintain persistent compute availability and handle variable workloads tied to real-time decision-making. Task execution also means the system incurs cost per action taken, not per prompt answered, creating different scaling economics. The capabilities listed—web browsing, research, design, image generation, music generation—suggest the product coordinates multiple specialized models, each with its own compute footprint.

The data does not reveal Manus AI's infrastructure choices, deployment model, or whether it runs on its own servers or rents compute from cloud providers. It does not show usage volumes, which would indicate actual pressure on the power and building infrastructure this site tracks. Verification occurred in mid-2026, but no indication exists whether the company has achieved material adoption or remains early-stage. For those watching whether autonomous agents become a significant fraction of AI workload, this product exists but remains unquantified.

profile_text.body:
Manus AI is the company behind Manus, an autonomous AI agent it describes as "the action engine that goes beyond answers to execute tasks, automate workflows, and extend your human reach." The company was founded in 2025 and operates via manus.im. According to its own site, Manus is positioned not as a question-answering tool but as an execution layer, capable of operating across a range of surfaces including a web app, browser operator, email, Slack integration, and tools for research, design, slides, image generation, and music generation.

The site's held facts classify Manus under the Automation and Agents category and note it as an autonomous agent with high decision-influence, reflecting its design around taking actions rather than simply returning information. No litigation, patent filings, SEC disclosures, or MCP server registrations are recorded for the company at this time.
